src/application/services/ReserveSpotService.ts: `private issued = 0;` with `this.issued += 1;` and `new Reservation(`res-${this.issued}`, ...)` generates entity identity from in-memory service state. This belongs in the domain (an identity factory) or in infrastructure behind an outbound port.

Proper application responsibilities are present: orchestration through SpotRepository, ReservationRepository and PaymentPort, use of the domain methods clashesWith and priceFor, and returning a ReservationReceipt.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of what ReserveSpotService.reserve does is proper application-layer work. It gets spots and reservations through repository ports, calls domain behaviour (Reservation.clashesWith, spot.priceFor), authorises payment through PaymentPort, saves through ReservationRepository and returns a receipt DTO.

However, it also enforces a business invariant about the Reservation concept itself: a reservation must last between 1 and 24 hours. That is a domain rule. It belongs in the domain layer, for example in the Reservation constructor or a factory, so the rule holds wherever a Reservation is created. Here it sits only in this one use case. The service also builds entity identity from a mutable in-memory counter (`private issued` and `res-${this.issued}`). ID generation is either a domain concern or an infrastructure concern behind a port. As written, IDs reset when the process restarts and are not unique across instances. These responsibilities belong to other layer kinds, so the unit fails. Confidence is moderate because input validation in application services is sometimes accepted.
